verdict: Bank of America had one of its strongest quarters yet: revenue rose 15% to $31.6B, every business segment grew profit by double digits, and net income rose 27% to $9.1B.

segments.name: Net interest income
segments.note: The spread between what the bank earns on loans and investments and what it pays on deposits — its biggest single money source.

segments.name: Noninterest income
segments.note: Fees and markets income: asset management fees, investment banking fees and sales & trading revenue of $7.1B.

flow.costPlain: Money set aside for loans expected to go bad — the closest thing a bank has to a cost of goods sold.

opex.name: Compensation and benefits
opex.note: Pay and benefits for the bank's roughly 213,000 employees — well over half of all running costs.

opex.name: Information processing and communications
opex.note: Technology, data processing and communications — the plumbing of a digital bank.

opex.name: Occupancy and equipment
opex.note: Branches, offices, ATMs and the equipment in them.

opex.name: Product delivery and transaction related
opex.note: The cost of moving money: processing payments, producing cards and handling transactions.

opex.name: Marketing
opex.note: Advertising and promoting the bank's products.

opex.name: Other general operating
opex.note: Everything else that does not fit the lines above.

takeaways.title: Growth everywhere at once
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 15% and every segment — consumer, wealth, global banking and markets — grew net income by double digits. Investment banking fees rose 50% and equities trading revenue rose 70%.

takeaways.title: Efficiency improved sharply
takeaways.text: The efficiency ratio improved to 59% from 63% a year ago: revenue grew much faster than the $18.6B of expenses, a 6.6% operating-leverage gain.

takeaways.title: Shareholders got paid
takeaways.text: The bank returned about $8B to shareholders in the quarter through dividends and buybacks, while its CET1 capital ratio stayed strong at 11.2%.

oneTimers: Preferred stock dividends of $326M sit between net income ($9,074M) and the $8,748M applicable to common shareholders.
